acv.quote: A hundred and eighty K a year, on a three-year term.

data.reason: A Fetchwell engineer built a working sitter payment flow over a weekend, which turned a bake-off into a win. Priya called it clean, but PayPal, Venmo and saved-card questions stayed open.

trigger.action: Lead with ending the engineering time spent keeping payments running.
trigger.why: Fetchwell was launching Canada and the UK while two engineers spent nearly full-time keeping sitter payments working.
trigger.quote: Two engineers more or less full-time just keeping sitter payments working.

decider.action: Aim the main message at the head of engineering, not finance.
decider.why: Daniel, VP of Engineering, signed. The CFO joined for ten minutes and asked one question.
decider.quote: this is an engineering decision, finance will sign what I bring them.

competitor.action: Say plainly what happens to PayPal, Venmo and saved cards.
competitor.why: After Fetchwell met Braintree, the questions turned to what they would lose. Priya only guesses Braintree caused it.
competitor.quote: It went from 'how fast can we build this' to 'what do we lose.'

message.action: Cut the average approval uplift claim for small-booking apps.
message.why: The acceptance-rate slide got silence. Daniel said 38 dollar bookings made approval rates a non-issue.
message.quote: our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates.

proof.action: Add a customer story of moving saved cards at Fetchwell's size.
proof.why: Daniel asked for one and never got it. The worry came up again at kickoff.
proof.quote: who's done this at our size without losing cards?

words.action: Say 'sitter pay' and 'paid by Friday' instead of 'payouts'.
words.why: Fetchwell's promise to sitters is 'paid by Friday'. The CFO's only question was about when sitters get paid.
words.quote: does this change when sitters get paid?
